LESSON: SELECTIVE LISTENING, IMITATIVE SPEAKING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: Listening and Speaking Listening for gist Imitative Speaking Phonological awaren
Topic 1.1: Selective Listening, Imitative speaking

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Selective Listening, Imitative speaking. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: how formal greetings are done in How do you get all the needed information from a listening text?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify specific information from given texts
2. apply appropriate language structures in communication
3. appreciate the value of greetings in fostering respect

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SELECTIVE LISTENING, IMITATIVE SPEAKING
Subject: GERMAN · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Selective Listening, Imitative speaking helps you succeed in GERMAN. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: SELECTIVE LISTENING, IMITATIVE SPEAKING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify specific information from given texts

What this means
In this part you learn to identify specific information from given texts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify specific information from given texts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Selective Listening, Imitative speaking”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify specific information from given texts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Apply appropriate language structures in communication

What this means
In this part you learn to apply appropriate language structures in communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply appropriate language structures in communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Selective Listening, Imitative speaking to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply appropriate language structures in communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the value of greetings in fostering respect

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the value of greetings in fostering respect. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the value of greetings in fostering respect.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the value of greetings in fostering respect. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Selective Listening, Imitative speaking is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Selective Listening, Imitative speaking”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify specific information from given texts)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Selective Listening, Imitative speaking to a partner. (skill: apply appropriate language structures in communication)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the value of greetings in fostering respect)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Selective Listening, Imitative speaking to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify specific information from given texts.
3. Practise this skill: apply appropriate language structures in communication.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the value of greetings in fostering respect.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Selective Listening, Imitative speaking from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Selective Listening, Imitative speaking: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Selective Listening, Imitative speaking?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. how formal greetings are done in How do you get all the needed information from a listening text?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Selective Listening, Imitative speaking means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify specific information from given texts.
5. Be able to: apply appropriate language structures in communication.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
